A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 32-page versions of MONET with complete main text and Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to pages 1, 5 and 11; all appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, expert-masking experiments, toxicity measurements and ablations, including Tables 2–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, knowledge-unlearning analyses, ablations and qualitative multimodal examples.

M1.justification: Equation 17 changes both ambiguity-loss coefficients from negative to positive 1/(2H), revising the written auxiliary training objective. The architecture and routing procedures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or models were retrained.

E1.justification: Both retain the same language and code training data, language benchmarks, MMLU domain masking, MultiPL-E evaluations, toxicity tests and vision-language examples. Coverage in Appendices B–F is identical.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: Table 2 retains LLAMA, OLMoE and Gemma 2 with and without Gemma Scope, while Figure 3 and Appendix E retain the same masking comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported model sizes, training budgets, zero-shot and five-shot settings, masking thresholds, generation procedures and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Appendices B–D contain identical experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same auxiliary-loss-weight and routing-group ablations. The expert-specialization, masking, toxicity and qualitative case studies in the main text and appendices are also unchanged.

E5.justification: No seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests are added or removed. Existing statistical aggregation and Pearson-correlation reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples are identical, including the main benchmark and toxicity tables, Table 7's ambiguity-loss ablation and Appendix E's full performance tables. Equation 17's correction is not accompanied by revised results.

T1.justification: The sign correction in Equation 17 substantively changes the mathematical definition of ambiguity loss. With the positive auxiliary weight used in Equation 18, minimizing it now favors larger maximum routing probabilities, matching the existing explanation. Appendix A's derivations and complexity calculations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about 262,144 experts per layer, square-root parameter scaling, monosemantic specialization and knowledge manipulation while preserving general performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the basic expert-selection criteria, missing quantitative evaluation of automated interpretability and restriction of knowledge manipulation to unlearning. The explanation of the ambiguity loss is also retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3's implementation snippets, Appendix B's hyperparameters and hardware, Appendix D's evaluation instructions, and the code/checkpoint access information are unchanged. No implementation update is documented alongside the loss-formula correction.

R1.justification: No cited research is added or removed. Positioning relative to sparse autoencoders, conventional mixture-of-experts architectures and PEER remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 revises author-role markers, adds a corresponding-author footnote and expands the funding acknowledgment to include NIPA/MSIT support. The scientific prose and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional author footnote slightly shifts first-page content, including Table 1, and the expanded acknowledgment changes spacing on page 11. Figure and table designs, captions and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation 17 resolves a contradiction between the printed objective and its stated purpose: minimization now encourages confident expert routing. This improves mathematical correctness and guidance for implementation. The empirical evidence and appendices are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish retraining or performance gains.
